verdict: Caution: lend selectively in Bhavnagar CPD only to small-ticket, domestic or non-US-linked units with tight stock-and-receivable control; avoid US-export-dependent cutters and polishers until tariff clarity returns.
title: Bhavnagar Cut & Polished Diamonds: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Bhavnagar CPD unit buys rough, gets it cut and polished by job-work artisans, and sells polished stones to wholesalers and traders, mostly for export.** Cash is tied in rough inventory and in receivables from a handful of buyers; the factory itself is cheap (imported saws, bruting and polishing wheels), so the real funding need is working capital, not capex. Pricing power is thin: the segment is fragmented and low value-addition, so profitability stays modest and forex moves hit directly [9]. **So when a proposal lands, check the rough-to-polished conversion margin and the buyer list first; if the top three buyers exceed 61% of revenue, ask for the buyer-wise ageing and a plan to diversify [8].**

## What has broken now
**Bhavnagar is in a visible downturn: more than 50 diamond factories have shut and artisans are leaving in large numbers ahead of Diwali [2], and local reporting on 29-Oct-2026 describes the industry in recession [1].** The trigger is external: US tariff hikes of up to 50% on Indian diamonds hit Gujarat's cutting and polishing hubs, with nearly one lakh workers affected [3]. Peer survey work found more than 75% of CPD players expecting volume impact from US tariffs, with cost pass-through the key monitorable [4]. **Note the dates: [3] is Aug-2025 and [4] is a June-2025 channel check, so treat them as the cause, not the current state; collect from customer the latest US order book and tariff rate actually being paid.**

## Where the growth is
**Gujarat's local demand signal is the strongest thing in the pack: GST collections up 11.9% Apr-to-date versus India's 6.1% [D], and electricity demand up 11.0% versus 9.5% [D].** India-wide, CPD output (IIP NIC 32) is up only 3.2% YoY [D], so the state is running ahead of the national segment. Peer commentary points to festival and wedding demand and organised retail expansion supporting the domestic side [6], and certification intensity is rising [7]. **Pursue domestic-jewellery-linked polishers, small-ticket studded-jewellery units selling in India [11], and units with certified-stone workflows; avoid pure US-export cutters with single-buyer concentration.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure every new line as a stock-and-book-debt facility with a drawing power against pledged polished stock, not a clean limit.** Take monthly stock statements, buyer-wise sales and receivable ageing, and the rough purchase register; reconcile GST returns to sales every month. **If operating margin slips below 3% or revenue falls sharply, treat it as a rating-action trigger and cut limits [10]; if gearing rises on higher debtors or inventory, ask for the inventory ageing before any enhancement [10].** Keep tenors short and insist on forex hedging where export receivables exist [9].

## Early-warning signs
**Watch factory shutdowns and artisan migration in the Bhavnagar cluster [2], and any widening of the India credit-to-output gap (bank credit +33.0% YoY versus output +3.8% [D]) that signals borrowed stock building.** A buyer payment delay beyond agreed terms, or a customer asking to substitute rough inventory for cash margin, is the exit signal.
